status: DEMO — check every 'unverified' or 'secondary' value against BS 7671 A4 / On-Site Guide 9th Ed before real use

_tags.verified_current: official current source (IET / BSI / NICEIC / PUCSL / CEB regs)
_tags.verified_2008_guide: ECA Guide to the Wiring Regulations (17th Ed, 2008) — concept OK, value may have changed
_tags.secondary: non-official site or manufacturer datasheet that quotes BS 7671 — likely right, not authoritative

supply._source_supply: verified_current — Sri Lanka Electricity (Safety, Quality & Continuity) Regulations 2016, Reg 50
supply._source_earthing: verified (Sri Lankan source) — Univ. of Moratuwa EE101 notes: 'The TT System of earthing is the one used in Sri Lanka'. Still a project input; SQCR Reg 64 lets the consumer ask the licensee (CEB/LECO) for earthing type and external Ze.
supply._note: ze/pfc are project inputs; null => WARNING

tt._source: RA x IΔn <= 50 V (411.5.3) and 200 ohm note: verified_2008_guide D7.5; 1667 ohm: secondary (squote); UoM notes say Sri Lankan electrodes may exceed 100 ohm

required_for.SOCKET_LE_32A: 18th Ed: sockets <= 32 A, no risk-assessment exception for dwellings — secondary (IET 18th Ed impact paper, draft stage); 2008 was <= 20 A (verified_2008_guide D7.1)
required_for.CONCEALED_LT_50MM: verified_2008_guide D7.1; 18th Ed reg no. 522.6.202/203 unverified
required_for.LIGHTING_DOMESTIC: secondary — IET 18th Ed impact paper (411.3.4, draft stage)

types.B: AC + pulsating + smooth DC (needed for PV/EV grid side)

rcd._source_design: verified_2008_guide D7.3, D7.4; Type B for PV/BESS: verified_current (PUCSL RTSPV-BESS framework)

max_zs_ohm._rule: Zs_max = Cmin x U0 / Ia, Cmin = 0.95 (verified_current: IET Wiring Matters 2023). 18th Ed values = 2008 values x 0.95.
max_zs_ohm._source_measured: 0.8 factor for measured Zs: verified_current (IET Wiring Matters 2023, Appendix 3) + verified_2008_guide C4.6.4

min_cpc_mm2_with_mcb._source: verified_2008_guide Table E4.5 — so reduced-cpc T&E is OK with MCBs

cables._type: 70C thermoplastic flat twin & earth (6242Y), Table 4D5, copper

1.0._source: verified_2008_guide App 2 (Table 4D5 sample); C/A/mV also secondary (cable datasheets)

1.5._source: A, C, mV, cpc: secondary (Farnell + Rapid datasheets citing 17th Ed Table 4D5); 100-103 unverified

2.5._source: Iz: verified_2008_guide Table C9.1; mV: secondary (datasheets)

6.0._source: A, C, mV, cpc: secondary (datasheets); 100-103 unverified

10.0._source: A, C, mV, cpc: secondary (datasheets); 100-103 unverified

ca_ambient_pvc70._source: 30 = reference (verified_2008_guide C4.3.5); 40 = 0.87 secondary (open-exam-prep); 35/40 bracket secondary (IET forum); 25/45/50 unverified

circuit_templates._note: max_length_m from 2008 Guide Table C9.2 (B-type, TN, 5%/3% VD) — sanity check only. TT + RCD not covered by that table.
circuit_templates._area_source: 100 m2 ring: secondary (Wikipedia, open-exam-prep) + UoM EE101 notes; 50/75 m2 radials: secondary (open-exam-prep)

ring_rules.unfused_spur_max: one single or one twin socket
ring_rules._source: verified_2008_guide C11.2 (433.1.4); 18th Ed reg 433.1.204 secondary (Wikipedia, IET forum)

earthing_bonding._source: verified_2008_guide E6.3–E6.5, E7; pink FE: verified_current (NICEIC A4)

sockets._source_type: verified_current (PUCSL single plug/socket standard; Sunday Times 2015)
sockets._source_height: verified_2008_guide D11 (UK Building Regs Part M — not a Sri Lankan rule)

lighting_design._purpose: Used by LayoutDesigner to decide HOW MANY lights and switches per room. Not part of BS 7671 (BS 7671 has no lux levels).

target_lux._source: unverified — commonly cited residential ranges (CIBSE/IES-style), picked mid-range: living 150–300, bedroom 100–150, kitchen 300 / worktop 500, bathroom 150–200, study 300–500, corridor/stairs 100, garage 50–100. Sri Lankan SLSEA code has illuminance tables (2009 Tables 2.10/2.11) but values were not extracted.

lumen_method.formula: total_lm = E * A / (UF * MF); N = max(1, round(A / 6)); lamp = smallest option with lumens >= total_lm / N; if none, use brightest and N = ceil(total_lm / its lumens)
lumen_method.rule: Fix the number of points from room size (~1 per 6 m2), then pick the smallest lamp that meets the lux target.
lumen_method._source: unverified — standard lumen method. UF 0.6 assumes small room, light-coloured walls/ceiling, LED fittings (typical UF range 0.4–0.7); MF 0.8 typical for LED in clean domestic rooms. Lamp lumens typical; datasheet overrides.
lumen_method._rule_source: lumen method: standard (unverified defaults); 1 point per 6 m2: design choice

power_density_check._source: verified (Sri Lankan source) — SLSEA Code of Practice for Energy Efficient Buildings 2009, Table 2.1 'Multifamily' 7.5 W/m². Code excludes single-family houses, so use as a benchmark only, never ERROR.

switching.switch_location: inside room, next to the door (latch side)
switching.outdoor_lights: photo-sensor or timer, with manual override
switching._source: one switch per space, no gang switching, outdoor photo/timer: verified (Sri Lankan source) — SLSEA 2009 code (mandatory for buildings it covers; good practice for houses). Door-side and two-way locations: design choice.

circuit_limits.split_rule: Use at least 2 lighting circuits per house so one trip doesn't black out the whole home; put bathroom lighting on a circuit shared with an adjoining room
circuit_limits._source: max points: design choice. Split rule: 📘 Guide C10.2 / G2.3 (avoid inconvenience; bathroom RCD nuisance-trip advice).

max_demand._purpose: Check the whole house against the main switch / supply after every change
max_demand._source_main_switch: verified (Sri Lankan source) — UoM EE101: single-phase main switch 'likely not to exceed 30A'. Project input: user should enter actual rating.
max_demand.method: Ib_total = sum(category demand) / 230; compare with main_switch_a

SOCKETS.rule: 100% of largest socket circuit's estimated load + 40% of every other socket circuit's estimated load
SOCKETS._note: Uses estimated load, not device rating. Rating-based (OSG-style) gives 36 A for 3 socket circuits, which fails every 30 A house. 200 W/outlet is a design choice.

AC._note: design choice — hot climate, ACs run together

WATER_HEATER_INSTANT.rule: 100% of largest + 100% of second largest + 25% of the rest

diversity._source: unverified — On-Site Guide-style domestic diversity from model knowledge; 📘 Guide C3.3 confirms diversity is used only for max demand. Verify in On-Site Guide 9th Ed Appendix A.

suggested_fixes: Ask CEB/LECO about a higher-rated single-phase or a three-phase supply
Stagger heavy loads (e.g. storage water heater on a timer)
Reduce AC count or choose inverter units with lower running current
max_demand._note_three_phase: verified_current (PUCSL): three-phase wiring needs a chartered engineer's design — say this when suggesting three-phase

typical_loads_w._source: planning defaults, not from a standard — user value overrides

bathroom_701._source: RCD, zones, IP, bonding: verified_2008_guide G2; 2.5 m: secondary (IET forum on A2 draft text of 701.512.3; 2008 value was 3 m)
